I’ll fight for affordable health care, fair housing, and policies that lift Oregon’s hardworking residents out of the special‑interest trap that has left our district under‑represented and out of touch. Join me, and together we’ll restore the courage and conviction that define Oregon, ensuring that our voice—not the lobbyists’—is heard in the halls of Congress.

I’m running for Congress not to chase the endless politics of Washington or the interests of Wall Street, but to put the needs of our communities front and center—protecting American jobs, restoring manufacturing to our own soil, ending unfair trade deals that drain our resources, and securing our borders so that families like mine can thrive. My experience as a senior advisor and acting associate commissioner in the Trump administration, where I trimmed costs and streamlined the Social Security Administration, demonstrates my commitment to fiscal responsibility and efficient governance. As vice‑president of government relations for the U.S. Business & Industry Council, I fought for a robust U.S. manufacturing base, and as a senior speechwriter under President Bush, I learned the power of clear, principled messaging. I hold graduate degrees from Wheaton College and Westminster Theological Seminary, and I have spent my life serving in public office, writing on trade deficits, infrastructure, defense, and the dangers of outsourcing and mass immigration. My wife Mary Alice, our three children, a daughter‑in‑law, and two grandsons are the heart of my life, and I promise to bring that same family‑first mindset to Congress. Together, we can make South Jersey great again—by putting conservative values, hard‑working Americans, and the future of our region above the politics of the elite. Thank you.

Friends of Cherry Hill, Erlton, Ocean City, and the entire South Jersey 2nd District, my name is Robert W. Patterson, and I am running to become the voice of our community—an economy built on hard work, family values, and the American spirit of self‑reliance. Born and raised in the Erlton neighborhood, I know our neighborhoods, our beaches, and the challenges our workers face—whether they are manufacturing veterans, small‑business owners, or families striving to keep their homes and jobs. With 40 years of marriage, three children, and two beloved grandsons, I understand the importance of a future that protects American jobs, restores our manufacturing base, eliminates unfair trade deals and mass outsourcing, and secures our borders—so our children can thrive. My experience as a senior advisor in the Trump administration—where I cut costs and streamlined the Social Security Administration—combined with my leadership at the U.S. Business & Industry Council, has given me the tools to fight for conservative principles and deliver real, measurable results. I have written and spoken on the urgency of reducing trade deficits, rebuilding infrastructure, strengthening defense, and ending the flood of mass immigration that threatens our way of life. I pledge to bring that same dedication to Washington, ensuring that the needs of South Jersey come first, not the agendas of Washington or Wall Street. Let’s make South Jersey great again—by restoring jobs, protecting families, and upholding the values that make our region proud. Vote for Robert W. Patterson—your local, conservative champion in Congress.

When I earned my scholarship to Pepperdine University—studying business, economics and international affairs—I also served on Nancy Reagan’s White House Advance Team, gaining firsthand insight into how Washington can be both powerful and efficient. Back in Pennsylvania I founded Amish Country Gazebos, building it into the nation’s leading custom gazebo retailer and creating generations of jobs for Central Pennsylvania workers. My 30‑year track record of launching and growing small businesses, combined with years of volunteer service with the Rotary, Junior Achievement, the United Way, the Salvation Army, the Boy Scouts, and the Lancaster Bible College board, has shown me that real progress is made when private‑sector ingenuity meets public‑sector purpose. I will bring that same common‑sense, results‑oriented approach to Washington: protecting taxpayers, cutting wasteful spending, championing small‑business growth, and investing in the families and communities that make Pennsylvania great. I ask for your vote so we can build a stronger, more prosperous future—one that keeps hard‑working Pennsylvanians at the center of our nation’s success.

Good evening, friends and neighbors of Central Pennsylvania. I am Chester “Chet” Beiler, a sixth‑generation Pennsylvanian who grew up on a 100‑acre dairy farm in Gap, where a devastating fire in the early 1980s taught me that resilience and hard work are the only safety nets when life throws a curveball. After dropping out to keep my family afloat, I returned to school, earned a scholarship to Pepperdine University—where I studied business, economics, and international affairs—and even served on Nancy Reagan’s White House Advance Team, learning firsthand how to make decisions that matter. Today, as the founder of Amish Country Gazebos, the nation’s leading retailer of custom‑built gazebos, and a champion of dozens of local businesses, I’ve created jobs for my neighbors and learned that a private‑sector mindset delivers results faster and more efficiently than bureaucratic red tape. My commitment to volunteerism—through Rotary, Junior Achievement, the Boy Scouts, and the United Way—has kept my heart in the community, and my board service at Lancaster Bible College has kept me grounded in faith and service. If elected, I will bring that same common‑sense, results‑oriented approach to Washington, protecting taxpayers by cutting wasteful spending, fostering a climate where small businesses thrive, and ensuring that every dollar of your tax money is spent on real, tangible progress for our families and our communities.

The wait time has now been dramatically reduced from up to 2  years to just 15 days in most cases. As of today, Harrys policy has helped over 1,080,000 men in America.

Harry is the Vice President of the Community Assistance Network, which is the largest non-profit organization in Baltimore County that helps families and individuals, who are homeless, go from dependency to independence.

In 2016 and 2018, Harry partnered with Habitat for Humanity and traveled to Haiti to study their disaster relief efforts after Haitis horrific earth quake of 2010 and then to Malawi, Africa to build homes for impoverished families in Lilongwe.

Harry received his Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Morgan State University. He than went on to receive his Masters of Public Administration in Public Policy from the University of Baltimore.

My commitment to the environment naturally evolved into a commitment to people: I’ve served in leadership roles with the Sumter County Democratic Party and the Young Democrats of South Carolina, fought relentlessly for voting rights as a dedicated poll manager, testified on legislation at the Statehouse, and championed youth engagement in every step of the political process. I live here with my partner Cat and our beloved pets, and when I’m not campaigning, I travel to historic sites, savor new foods, cheer on the Buffalo Bills, and keep my sneaker collection fresh—because I believe that a leader must be connected to the everyday joys and challenges of the community. I am running to ensure that every resident—regardless of income, background, or species—has a seat at the table and a voice that matters. Together, we can protect our environment, empower our communities, and build a South Carolina that works for all of us. Join me, and let’s make that vision a reality.

Dear neighbors of Sumter and the surrounding communities, I am Kevin Eckert, a Rochester native turned South Carolina resident, whose career began in wildlife research at the Savannah River Ecology Lab and evolved into a frontline role with USDA Wildlife Services, managing beaver‑related issues across Clarendon, Calhoun, Sumter, and Lee counties. My love for the environment grew into a commitment to give a voice to the overlooked—leading the Sumter County Democratic Party, the Young Democrats of South Carolina, and fighting for voting rights as a poll manager on election day. I volunteer with SC Audubon and Conservation Voters of South Carolina, testify on the Statehouse to protect our natural resources, and champion youth engagement in politics. Living in Sumter with my partner Cat, our three cats and two snakes, I know the everyday concerns of small‑town residents and the power of community. If you’re looking for a candidate who will fight for the environment, the underserved, and the next generation, let’s build a South Carolina that listens and thrives together. Vote Kevin Eckert—your advocate for a greener, more inclusive future.
